In this repo (the framework is `tessel`), it happens in four steps:

1. **Collecting the methods when the class is defined.** You subclass `VerbView` (`src/tessel/views.py:138`). Its `__init_subclass__` (`views.py:165`) checks the class for any names in `http_method_funcs` (`views.py:11`: get, post, put, …). If the class doesn't set `methods` itself, it sets `cls.methods` to those names in uppercase, plus any methods inherited from base classes. A class with `get()` and `post()` ends up with `{"GET", "POST"}`.

2. **Turning the class into a function.** `View.to_view_func(name, *args, **kwargs)` (`views.py:85`) builds a plain `view(**kwargs)` function.
   - By default, each call creates a new instance and calls `self.run_view(**kwargs)`.
   - If `init_every_request = False`, one instance is created up front and reused for every request.
   - It applies any `decorators` set on the class.
   - It attaches `view_class`, `__name__`, `methods` and `provide_automatic_options` to the function.

3. **Registering the route.** `attach_route_rule` (`src/tessel/sansio/app.py:606`) uses `view_func.methods` as the route's allowed methods when you don't pass `methods=` (`sansio/app.py:622-623`). If you don't set `provide_automatic_options`, OPTIONS is added automatically.

4. **Handling a request.**
   - `Tessel.run_view` (`src/tessel/app.py:966`) looks up the endpoint and calls the view function with the URL variables (`app.py:990`).
   - That calls `VerbView.run_view` (`views.py:182`), which does `getattr(self, request.method.lower())` to pick `get` or `post`. A HEAD request falls back to `get`.
   - The chosen method runs through `active_app.ensure_sync`, so async handlers work too.

The base `View` class has none of this per-method routing: you override `run_view` yourself.
